challengers.bio: Junaid Ahmed is a community activist and proud son of immigrants with a computer science degree from DePaul University and an MBA from the University of Chicago. He previously ran for Congress in IL-8 in 2022 and is now running again to challenge incumbent Raja Krishnamoorthi in the 2026 Democratic primary, endorsed by Reps. Ro Khanna and Delia Ramirez.
challengers.name: Junaid Ahmed
challengers.ourTake: Ahmed lists "Peace in Gaza and Palestinian self-determination" as a top campaign priority and calls the situation a genocide. His advocacy against U.S.-Israel policy dates to 2021, when he condemned U.S. tax dollars "going towards oppressing the Palestinian people." Endorsed by Ro Khanna and refusing corporate PAC money, he represents the kind of Muslim-American representation MUPAC is fighting for.

challengers.bio: Son of immigrants with a Georgetown Law degree and UVA MBA, running for Texas' 33rd Congressional District. A proud American Muslim who built his career expanding telehealth access, mentoring youth, and supporting nonprofits. Advised Congress on labor rights at the Harrison Institute and worked at the World Trade Organization in Geneva.
challengers.name: Zeeshan Hafeez
challengers.ourTake: Hafeez explicitly calls for ending AIPAC and foreign lobby control in Washington, formally recognizing the state of Palestine, and stopping taxpayer dollars from "funding genocide abroad." As a Muslim-American progressive in Texas, he champions Palestinian dignity and opposes unconditional military aid to Israel. His victory would bring a powerful new voice for Palestine to Congress.

challengers.bio: Kat Abughazaleh (Kat Abu) is a 25-year-old Palestinian-American journalist, social media influencer, and political commentator whose family originates from Gaza and Bethlehem. She rose to prominence at Media Matters for America criticizing Tucker Carlson and is now running for Congress in Illinois' 9th District to replace retiring Rep. Jan Schakowsky, having raised over $350,000 from nearly 11,000 small-dollar donors.
challengers.name: Kat Abughazaleh
challengers.ourTake: A proud Palestinian-American whose grandparents survived the Nakba, Abughazaleh calls for a comprehensive ceasefire, complete Israeli military withdrawal from Gaza, and U.S. recognition of the State of Palestine. She slept on concrete outside the 2024 DNC protesting the exclusion of Palestinian voices. If elected, she would be the youngest woman and second Palestinian-American ever in Congress—a transformative voice for the Muslim community.

challengers.bio: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed is a physician, epidemiologist, and former Wayne County Health Director who previously ran for Michigan Governor in 2018. He is running for U.S. Senate in Michigan's 2026 race to fill retiring Senator Gary Peters' seat, with endorsements from Bernie Sanders, Ro Khanna, and Keith Ellison. His campaign focuses on healthcare for all, affordable housing, economic justice, and sensible foreign policy.
challengers.name: Abdul El-Sayed
challengers.ourTake: Endorsed by Bernie Sanders and backed by Michigan's Arab American community, El-Sayed calls Israel's conduct in Gaza a genocide and supports the Uncommitted Movement. He is running to be the first pro-Palestine Senator from Michigan and would bring a principled voice for human rights and diplomacy to the Senate. His victory would be transformative for Muslim-American political representation.

challengers.bio: Ethiopian-American attorney and PhD student who was fired from Sidley Austin for speaking out against the law firm's stance on Gaza. Immigrated to Denver from Tigray, Ethiopia in 1998, holds degrees from Washington College and Notre Dame Law School, and is now challenging 28-year incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette with Justice Democrats' endorsement.
challengers.name: Melat Kiros
challengers.ourTake: Kiros lost her law job for defending the right to criticize Israeli government actions—and turned that injustice into a Congressional campaign. She calls for ending U.S. military aid to Israel and an arms embargo, drawing on her family's experience fleeing genocide in Tigray. Justice Democrats-endorsed and explicitly pro-ceasefire, she represents exactly the courageous leadership MUPAC seeks.

challengers.bio: Donavan McKinney is a Michigan State Representative from Detroit who grew up in poverty, experiencing 13 evictions before becoming the first in his family to graduate college. A former SEIU organizer and Climate Power political director, he is running for Congress in Michigan's 13th District with endorsements from Rashida Tlaib, Bernie Sanders, and Justice Democrats to challenge self-funded incumbent Shri Thanedar.
challengers.name: Donavan McKinney
challengers.ourTake: Endorsed by Rashida Tlaib and Justice Democrats, McKinney is a priority candidate for MUPAC. He co-sponsored Michigan's state resolution urging Congress to block arms to Israel and provide aid to Gaza, directly aligning with Tlaib's federal efforts. His progressive credentials and solidarity with Palestinian rights make him essential for expanding the pro-Palestine caucus in Congress.

challengers.bio: Durham County Commissioner and first Muslim woman elected to public office in North Carolina. Motivated by the 2015 Chapel Hill murders of three Muslim students who were her friends, Allam served as Bernie Sanders' NC political director in 2016 and is now challenging Rep. Valerie Foushee in a rematch of their 2022 primary.
challengers.name: Nida Allam
challengers.ourTake: Nida Allam is a top-tier MUPAC candidate. AIPAC spent nearly $2.5 million against her in 2022. She has called Israel's actions in Gaza genocide, refuses all AIPAC and corporate PAC money, and explicitly criticizes Foushee's silence on the war. Endorsed by Bernie Sanders, Justice Democrats, and Working Families Party, she represents the gold standard for Palestine solidarity candidates.

challengers.bio: Chris Rabb is a 5-term Pennsylvania State Representative from Philadelphia's 200th District, former Temple University professor, and Yale/UPenn graduate. He has worked as an aide to Senator Carol Moseley Braun and at the White House Conference on Small Business. He is running for Congress in Pennsylvania's 3rd District to replace retiring Rep. Dwight Evans, focusing on educational justice, decarceration, and environmental sustainability.
challengers.name: Chris Rabb
challengers.ourTake: Chris Rabb is a standout MUPAC ally who called for a ceasefire just 11 days after October 7, 2023. He is working on state legislation to divest Pennsylvania from Israel bonds and investments. He spoke at Gaza peace vigils, visited pro-Palestine encampments to support student protesters, and was the only elected official to attend Philadelphia's People's Tribunal on War Crimes in Gaza. His vocal advocacy makes him one of the most aligned candidates with Muslim community priorities on Palestine.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Rashida Tlaib represents Michigan's 12th Congressional District, serving since 2019. The first Palestinian-American woman elected to Congress and one of the first two Muslim women in Congress, she is a founding member of the Squad.
incumbents.name: Rashida Tlaib
incumbents.ourTake: The only Palestinian-American in Congress and MUPAC's most essential champion, Tlaib has endured censure for her unflinching defense of Palestinian rights. She introduced H.Res.876 recognizing genocide in Gaza with 20+ co-sponsors, calls for an arms embargo and sanctions on Israel, and refuses to attend any event honoring Netanyahu. Her voice in Congress is irreplaceable.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Delia Ramirez represents Illinois' 3rd Congressional District, serving since 2023. The first Latina elected to Congress from Illinois, she previously served in the Illinois General Assembly and is a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
incumbents.name: Delia Ramirez
incumbents.ourTake: A lead author of the Ceasefire Now Resolution introduced just 9 days after October 7, Ramirez also introduced the Block the Bombs Act to halt offensive weapons to Israel. She declared "Gaza is not for sale" after Trump's ethnic cleansing proposals and has voted against every unconditional aid package to Israel. A fearless freshman leader on Palestinian rights.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Ilhan Omar represents Minnesota's 5th Congressional District, serving since 2019. The first Somali-American elected to Congress and one of the first two Muslim women in Congress, she serves on the House Budget and Education committees.
incumbents.name: Ilhan Omar
incumbents.ourTake: The fiercest champion for Palestine in Congress, Omar called for an arms embargo immediately after October 7 and introduced the first resolution to block weapons sales to Israel. Endorsed by Justice Democrats and the Congressional Progressive Caucus, she won her 2024 primary by 14 points—proving that defending Palestinian rights is winning politics. Her return to Congress is essential for the Muslim community.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez represents New York's 14th Congressional District, serving since 2019. A former community organizer and the youngest woman elected to Congress at age 29, she serves on the House Financial Services and Oversight committees and is a leading progressive voice in the Democratic caucus.
incumbents.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
incumbents.ourTake: AOC was among the first to call Israel's assault on Gaza a genocide from the House floor, demanding a halt to offensive weapons transfers. She co-sponsored the Block the Bombs Act and H.Res.876 recognizing the genocide in Gaza. While navigating complex votes on defensive systems, she has consistently used her platform to amplify Palestinian suffering and demand accountability.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Andre Carson represents Indiana's 7th Congressional District, serving since 2008. One of the first two Muslims elected to Congress, he serves on the House Intelligence Committee and is a former law enforcement officer. He is a senior member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.
incumbents.name: Andre Carson
incumbents.ourTake: One of only three Muslim members of Congress, Carson co-led the Ceasefire Now Resolution and has championed UNRWA funding restoration to address the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. He secured $75 million in food assistance for Palestinian refugees with 63 Congressional colleagues. A steady, principled voice for Muslim and Palestinian communities in Congress.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Greg Casar represents Texas' 35th Congressional District, serving since 2023. A former Austin City Council member and labor organizer, he chairs the Congressional Progressive Caucus and is a member of the Squad.
incumbents.name: Greg Casar
incumbents.ourTake: As Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Casar led 20 members demanding Biden withhold offensive weapons from Israel. His district polling showed 80% of voters support his pro-ceasefire stance—proving Palestinian advocacy wins elections. He co-sponsored the Block the Bombs Act and genocide recognition resolution. A rising progressive leader showing that supporting Palestine is both moral and politically smart.

incumbents.bio: Sen. Chris Van Hollen represents Maryland in the U.S. Senate, serving since 2017. A member of the Senate Appropriations and Foreign Relations committees, he previously served 10 terms in the House of Representatives and was chairman of the DCCC.
incumbents.name: Chris Van Hollen
incumbents.ourTake: Called "the conscience of Congress" on Gaza, Van Hollen co-sponsored the first-ever Senate resolution for U.S. recognition of Palestinian statehood. He documented Israel's humanitarian law violations, visited the West Bank to witness settler violence firsthand, and pushed to condition military aid on compliance with U.S. law. A former reliable Israel supporter who found his moral voice on Gaza.

incumbents.bio: Sen. Bernie Sanders represents Vermont in the U.S. Senate, serving since 2007. The longest-serving independent in congressional history, he chairs the Senate HELP Committee and previously chaired the Budget Committee. He ran for president in 2016 and 2020.
incumbents.name: Bernie Sanders
incumbents.ourTake: The Senate's leading voice on Gaza, Sanders introduced historic resolutions to block arms sales to Israel—winning support from over half the Democratic caucus. The first Senator to officially call Israel's assault on Gaza a "genocide," he has demanded an immediate ceasefire and arms embargo while pushing for Palestinian self-determination. His moral authority on this issue is unmatched.

incumbents.bio: Cori Bush is a former Congresswoman and nurse from Missouri who was elected in 2020 as part of "The Squad" with Justice Democrats support. She lost her 2024 primary to Wesley Bell after AIPAC and allied groups spent $8.5 million against her. She is running in 2026 to reclaim Missouri's 1st District seat, focusing on economic justice, healthcare, and anti-war advocacy.
incumbents.name: Cori Bush
incumbents.ourTake: Bush introduced the first House ceasefire resolution just 10 days after October 7 and has explicitly called for ending U.S. consent for genocide in Gaza. AIPAC spent $8.5 million to defeat her in 2024 because of her Palestine advocacy—making her return to Congress a major victory for the movement. Her fight against the Israel lobby is a fight for the entire Muslim and progressive community.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Summer Lee represents Pennsylvania's 12th Congressional District, serving since 2023. The first Black woman elected to Congress from Pennsylvania, she previously served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives and is a member of the Squad.
incumbents.name: Summer Lee
incumbents.ourTake: Lee co-sponsored the ceasefire resolution within days of October 7 and has voted against every military aid package to Israel. Her crushing 21-point primary victory in 2024—despite $600K in attacks over her Gaza stance—proved her slogan right: "Opposing genocide is good politics and good policy." Representing historically Jewish Squirrel Hill, she shows progressive Palestine values can win anywhere.

incumbents.bio: Sen. Jeff Merkley represents Oregon in the U.S. Senate, serving since 2009. A member of the Senate Foreign Relations and Appropriations committees, he previously served as Speaker of the Oregon House of Representatives.
incumbents.name: Jeff Merkley
incumbents.ourTake: The second Senator ever to call for a ceasefire, Merkley co-introduced the historic resolution for U.S. recognition of Palestinian statehood. After traveling to Gaza's border in 2025, he called out Netanyahu's "vision of depopulating Gaza" and demanded the U.S. end complicity in the humanitarian catastrophe. A courageous voice pushing the Senate toward justice for Palestinians.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Ayanna Pressley represents Massachusetts' 7th Congressional District, serving since 2019. The first Black woman elected to Congress from Massachusetts, she serves on the House Financial Services Committee and is a founding member of the Squad.
incumbents.name: Ayanna Pressley
incumbents.ourTake: Pressley was among the first to call for a ceasefire and introduced amendments to block offensive weapons to Israel. She led 60 lawmakers opposing forced displacement of Palestinians, refused to attend Netanyahu's address—calling him a "war criminal"—and has stated plainly: "History will remember this moment as a genocide." A powerful moral voice in Congress.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Pramila Jayapal represents Washington's 7th Congressional District, serving since 2017. She previously served as chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and was a member of the Washington State Senate. She is the first South Asian American woman elected to the House.
incumbents.name: Pramila Jayapal
incumbents.ourTake: Jayapal called for ceasefire 10 days after October 7 and has led the legislative fight to block arms sales—introducing the Block the Bombs Act and multiple resolutions to halt nearly $4 billion in proposed weapons transfers. She skipped Netanyahu's Congressional address and stated that providing weapons while Israel violates international law "makes us complicit." A key architect of Congressional Palestine advocacy.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Adelita Grijalva represents Arizona's 7th Congressional District, serving since November 2025. The daughter of the late Rep. Raul Grijalva, she previously served on the Pima County Board of Supervisors and won a special election to succeed her father.
incumbents.name: Adelita Grijalva
incumbents.ourTake: Grijalva called for a ceasefire just 10 days after October 7 and has publicly stated that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza. Following in her father Raul's footsteps as a champion for progressive causes, she co-sponsored the Block the Bombs Act upon taking office. The first Latina to represent Arizona in Congress, she advocates for an immediate ceasefire and restoration of humanitarian aid.

incumbents.bio: Rep. Lateefah Simon represents California's 12th Congressional District, serving since January 2025. A civil rights leader and former BART Board Director, she is a close ally of Vice President Kamala Harris and succeeded Rep. Barbara Lee in Congress. She is the first Muslim member of Congress from California.
incumbents.name: Lateefah Simon
incumbents.ourTake: California's first Muslim member of Congress, Simon campaigned on pursuing an immediate ceasefire and has called Israeli actions "devastating, deplorable, and unacceptable." She strongly opposed Trump's proposal for U.S. control of Gaza, calling it "ethnic cleansing." Endorsed by AROC Action and bringing a powerful civil rights perspective to Palestinian advocacy, her historic election expands Muslim representation in Congress.
